desc:
The string s contains only the letters a, b and c. Count the subsequences of s that consist of at least one a, followed by at least one b, followed by at least one c (such as abc, aabbc or abcc).

Two subsequences are different if they use different sets of positions, even when they spell the same word. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

For example, s = "abc" gives 1, s = "aabc" gives 3 (the a-part is the first a, the second a or both, followed by the only b and c), and s = "cba" gives 0.
constraints: s consists only of the letters a, b and c
hints: Enumerating all subsequences is exponential. Try to count them as you scan the string once, using a few counters.
Keep three counters: the number of subsequences of the form a+, of the form a+b+, and of the form a+b+c+ seen so far.
On an a: A = 2A + 1 (extend each old one or not, or start a new one). On a b: B = 2B + A. On a c: C = 2C + B. The answer is C.
editorial: Let A, B, C be the number of subsequences of the prefix read so far that match the shapes a+, a+b+ and a+b+c+. Reading a new letter changes only one of them.

A new a can either extend any existing a+ subsequence (A of them), stay out of every old one (those remain, A more), or start a fresh subsequence consisting of just this a: A = 2A + 1. A new b can extend an existing a+b+ subsequence (B choices) or be placed after an a+ subsequence to begin the b-part (A choices), plus the old ones stay: B = 2B + A. Similarly C = 2C + B for a c. All values are kept modulo 1,000,000,007. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.
